local_entities.label: Federation type-2 phaser used in transaction

evidence.summary: Approaching the edge of his known region, Neelix seeks new shipboard skills while Janeway says Voyager will soon depend even more on his local knowledge.
Neelix tells Wix he fears his usefulness will end because he has never traveled beyond the Nekrit Expanse and asks for help obtaining a map.
Wix draws Neelix into a covert narcotics exchange using a Voyager phaser; the transaction turns violent and a participant is killed in self-defense.
Wix reveals the cargo was narcotics and pressures Neelix into silence by invoking their past debt, Neelix's hidden criminal involvement, and fear of losing Voyager.
The Federation phaser signature becomes evidence in the station investigation and suspicion falls on Voyager personnel who were not responsible for the killing.
Kolaati associates demand Voyager warp plasma; Neelix refuses to steal from the crew and Paris's account of his own downfall emphasizes that lying after a mistake compounded the harm.
Neelix and Wix confess their role and exonerate Chakotay and Paris, then offer Bahrat a plan to capture the Kolaati trafficking operation instead of stealing real Voyager plasma.
The trafficking sting succeeds after violence; Kolaati criminals are taken into custody, Chakotay and Paris are released, and Wix departs.
Janeway condemns Neelix's lies and breach of trust, rejects his offer to simply leave, says he has obligations as part of the Voyager family, and assigns two weeks of punitive maintenance.
Janeway tells Neelix that no one knows what lies ahead and that uncertainty itself does not make him useless to Voyager.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: Fear of becoming useless pushes Neelix into an old friend's criminal scheme, escalating from secrecy to trafficking and false suspicion before confession and a sting operation.
neutral_coding.epistemics: Initial suspicions from phaser evidence are preserved and later corrected by confession and direct criminal evidence.
neutral_coding.agency_institutions: Neelix's fear explains but does not erase his choices; Janeway treats trust violation, accountability, continued membership, and punishment as compatible.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: Neelix's lack of regional knowledge does not actually terminate his role aboard Voyager.
